arxiv-2206-01033.title: Quasi-exactly solvable extensions of the Kepler-Coulomb potential on the sphere
arxiv-2206-01033.creator: C. Quesne
arxiv-2206-01033.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by C. Quesne. We consider a family of extensions of the Kepler-Coulomb potential on a d d -dimensional sphere and analyze it in a deformed supersymmetric framework, wherein the starting potential is known to exhibit a deformed shape invariance property. We show that the members of the extended family are also endowed with such a property, provided some constraint conditions relating the potential parameters are satisfied, in other words they are conditionally deformed shape invariant.

arxiv-2207-08985.description: Abstract . We give an elementary construction of representing systems of the Cauchy kernels in the Hardy spaces H p H^{p} , 1 ≤ p < ∞ 1\leq p<\infty , as well as of representing systems of reproducing kernels in weighted Hardy spaces. 2000 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 30H20; Secondary 30D10, 30E05, 42C15, 94A20 1.

arxiv-2209-04208.title: The Steady States of Isotone Electric Systems
arxiv-2209-04208.creator: Dan Comănescu
arxiv-2209-04208.description: Abstract The steady states of an isotone electric system are described by an isotone function with respect to the componentwise order. When there are steady states, we highlight a dominant steady state and we study its domain of attraction for the fixed point iteration method.

arxiv-2308-01852.title: REU - Schwartz Functions and Compactifications
arxiv-2308-01852.creator: Jonah Marcus, Molly Sager
arxiv-2308-01852.description: Abstract In the early 20th century, Laurent Schwartz observed that we can identify functions that extend smoothly to the point at infinity of one-point compactifications of Euclidean spaces. We show a similar result for a different compactification of Euclidean spaces, namely, the real projective spaces.

arxiv-2311-13783.title: A Drude-Lorentz dielectric in the presence of a magnetic current density
arxiv-2311-13783.creator: Pedro D. S. Silva a, M. J. Neves b, Manoel M. Ferreira Jr. a,c
arxiv-2311-13783.description: Abstract The dispersive propagation and absorption in the domain of a Drude-Lorentz dielectric modified by a magnetic current are classically investigated, taking as the starting point the Drude electric permittivity, in connection with the chiral magnetic effect. Using standard electromagnetic methods, the dispersion relations and refractive indices are evaluated and discussed, as well as the group and the energy velocities.

arxiv-2408-02872.title: Rate-Splitting for Joint Unicast and Multicast Transmission in LEO Satellite Networks with Non-Uniform Traffic Demand
arxiv-2408-02872.creator: Jaehyup Seong, Juha Park, Dong-Hyun Jung, Jeonghun Park, Wonjae Shin
arxiv-2408-02872.description: Abstract Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications (SATCOM) with ubiquitous global connectivity is deemed a pivotal catalyst in advancing wireless communication systems for 5G and beyond. LEO SATCOM excels in delivering versatile information services across expansive areas, facilitating both unicast and multicast transmissions via high-speed broadband capability.

arxiv-2505-04816.title: On some relatively free pro- p p groups
arxiv-2505-04816.creator: Dan Segal
arxiv-2505-04816.description: Abstract 1 Introduction A group G is finitely axiomatizable (or FA ) in some class \mathcal{C} if G is determined up to isomorphism among all groups in \mathcal{C} by a single sentence in the first-order theory of groups (or, equivalently, by finitely many such sentences).

arxiv-2508-16797.title: Tripodal structure in undersaturated random graphs
arxiv-2508-16797.creator: William DiCarlo, Lorenzo Sadun
arxiv-2508-16797.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by William DiCarlo, Lorenzo Sadun. We numerically investigate typical graphs in a region of the Strauss model of random graphs with constraints on the densities of edges and triangles. This region, where typical graphs had been expected to be bipodal but turned out to be tripodal, involves edge densities e e below e 0 = ( 3 − 3 ) / 6 ≈ 0.2113 e_{0}=(3-\sqrt{3})/6\approx 0.2113 and triangle densities t t slightly below e 3 e^{3} .

arxiv-2602-15429.title: Deep description of static and dynamic network ties in Honduran villages
arxiv-2602-15429.creator: Marios Papamichalis, Nikolaos Nakis, Nicholas A. Christakis
arxiv-2602-15429.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Marios Papamichalis, Nikolaos Nakis, Nicholas A. Christakis. We examine static and dynamic social network structure in 176 villages within the Copán Department of Honduras across two data waves (2016, 2019), using detailed data on multiplex networks for 20,232 individuals enrolled in a longitudinal survey. These networks capture friendship, health advice, financial help, and adversarial relationships, allowing us to show how cooperation and conflict jointly shape social structure.

pmc-11637516.title: Validation of a questionnaire for central nervous system aspects of joint pain: the CAP questionnaire
pmc-11637516.creator: Daniel F McWilliams, Vasileios Georgopoulos, Jayamala Patel, Bonnie Millar, Stephanie L Smith, David A Walsh
pmc-11637516.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundNeuropathic-like pain, fatigue, cognitive difficulty, catastrophizing, anxiety, sleep disturbance, depression and widespread pain associate with a single factor in people with knee pain. We report the Central Aspects of Pain questionnaire (CAP) to characterize this across painful musculoskeletal conditions.MethodsCAP was derived from the 8-item CAP-Knee questionnaire, and completed by participants with joint pain in the Investigating Musculoskeletal Health and Wellbeing survey. Subgroups had OA, back pain or FM. Acceptability was evaluated by feedback and data missingness.

pmc-11684019.title: Unveiling the Antimycobacterial Potential of Novel 4-Alkoxyquinolines: Insights into Selectivity, Mechanism of Action, and In Vivo Exposure
pmc-11684019.creator: Fernanda
pmc-11684019.description: This work presents a comprehensive investigation into the design, synthesis, and evaluation of a novel series of 4-alkoxyquinolines as potential antimycobacterial agents. The design approach, which combined molecular simplification and chain extension, resulted in compounds with potent and selective activity against both drug-susceptible and multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains.

pmc-12374320.title: An uncommon case of neonatal asphyxia associated with infantile-onset Pompe disease
pmc-12374320.creator: Francesco Leo, Luca Barchi, Giulia Russo, Eleonora Balestri, Elena Chesi, Francesco Di Dio, Livia Garavelli, Lorenzo Iughetti, Giancarlo Gargano
pmc-12374320.description: BackgroundPompe disease, also known as glycogenosis type II or acid maltase deficiency, is an autosomal recessive disease caused by a deficiency of alpha-glucosidase. The severity depends mainly on the type of mutation, which in turn determines early or late onset; therapy modifies the outcome but does not alter the severity of the disease at presentation.

pmc-12468144.title: Ketogenic Diet and Thyroid Function: A Delicate Metabolic Balancing Act
pmc-12468144.creator: Petar Vranjić, Mladen Vuković, Senka Blažetić, Barbara Viljetić, Violeta Popovici
pmc-12468144.description: The ketogenic diet (KD), a high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet, causes profound metabolic adaptations that go beyond energy production and affect endocrine function and thyroid hormone regulation. By shifting the body’s primary fuel source from glucose to fatty acids and ketones, the KD alters insulin signaling, inflammation levels and deiodinase activity, which together affect thyroid hormone metabolism.

pmc-12627811.title: Desiccation cracking behavior of xanthan gum admixed clay
pmc-12627811.creator: Yuxia Bai, Meihui Cheng, Henglin Xiao, Lihua Li, Qiang Ma, Jun He, Yeping Yang, Yongfeng Deng
pmc-12627811.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study investigates the desiccation cracking properties of xanthan gum (XG)-treated clay and its effectiveness in repairing cracked clay by examining their evaporation characteristics, crack propagation, patterns, and the related micro-mechanisms were discussed with the aid of micro examination. Results show that (i) the evaporation rate curve of untreated and XG-treated clay exhibits a Z-shape with three stages, and the latter possesses higher water content, smaller evaporation rate, and longer evaporation durations.

pmc-12737602.creator: Alexandro Fritzen, Aleksandro Schafer da Silva, Yi Yang
pmc-12737602.description: Simple SummaryThe inflammatory state is constant in dairy cows and predisposes them to the development of diseases, with some paradigms being addressed in this review: (a) the involvement of axes such as GH/IGF-1 and ACTH/cortisol in the regulation of the inflammatory process; (b) modulation of the tissue macrophage profile, which demonstrates great potential in controlling inflammation, lipolysis, and improving energy

pmc-13039598.title: Clinical Outcomes of Cartilage Procedures Performed in Conjunction With Primary Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: A Systematic Review
pmc-13039598.creator: Napatpong Thamrongskulsiri, Logan D. Moews, Jacob T. Morgan, Felipe Casanova, Tomas F. Vega, Gabriel Octavio Pérez Lloveras, Adam B. Yanke, Brian J. Cole, Jorge Chahla
pmc-13039598.description: Background:Cartilage lesions are frequently encountered during anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) and may influence long-term outcomes. Surgical options include debridement, microfracture, osteochondral autograft transfer (OAT), osteochondral allograft transplantation (OCA), and autologous chondrocyte implantation (ACI), yet the optimal approach remains controversial.

pmc-13234115.title: Biofilms reshape soil-water dynamics with enhanced vapor adsorption and hysteresis reversal under dry conditions
pmc-13234115.creator: Huan Hu, Chong Chen, Yili Lu, Robert Horton, Tusheng Ren
pmc-13234115.description: Bacterial biofilms are crucial for microbial survival during drought by modifying soil-water dynamics. Their influence on water vapor transport in dry soils remains unexplored. This study systematically investigates biofilm-mediated changes in soil water vapor sorption (SWVS) dynamics across a wide matric potential range (−400 MPa to −10 MPa).

pmc-13235167.title: Selenoprotein P deficiency in MASLD: association with insulin resistance and liver fibrosis: a prospective case-control study
pmc-13235167.creator: Mona A Hegazy, Samar Saad Mohamed, Eman H Saad, Ahmed Abdelghani, Dalia Abd el Fattah, Mohamed Ahmed Elsayed Mekki, Mona Fathy, Nora Hassan, Omar Ashoush
pmc-13235167.description: Background & aimsMetabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a globally escalating health concern. Selenoprotein P (SEPP1) is a hepatokine involved in selenium transport and antioxidant defense, with conflicting data on its role in MASLD. This study investigated serum SEPP1 as a potential non-invasive biomarker for disease severity and fibrosis staging.

pmc-13587589.title: Bridging the gap: a genetically validated avian chorioallantoic membrane platform for investigation of spontaneous circulating tumor cells
pmc-13587589.creator: Dennis Roth, Rui P L Neves, Julia Geheb, Christian Ballmeyer, Nathalie Gaßmann, Kiki C Andree, Monica Sudarsanam, Christiane Driemel, Celine Örencik, Andrè Franken, Eslam Elmaghraby, Sven H Loosen, Roderburg Christoph, Sebastian Schoelch, Hans Neubauer, Wolfram T Knoefel, Nikolas H Stoecklein, Georg
pmc-13587589.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are clinically relevant markers of metastasis and prognosis in gastrointestinal (GI) cancers. However, their extreme rarity and the limitations of current in vivo models severely restrict mechanistic studies of tumor cell dissemination. Here, we demonstrate for the first time that the avian chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) assay can serve as a biologically relevant and ethically advantageous 3R‐compliant (Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement) in vivo model for investigating spontaneous CTC generation.

pmc-13633099.title: Integrative QTL mapping and transcriptomic profiling uncover molecular mechanisms underlying lodging resistance in Brassica napus
pmc-13633099.creator: Mingli Wu, Huaixin Li, Liyun Miao, Yutian Xia, Xinmin Liu, Xin Cheng, Jianshuo Li, Shipeng Fan, Dongqing Zhang, Xiaoling Dun, Maoteng Li
pmc-13633099.description: Lodging remains a significant agronomic challenge that limits the yield potential of Brassica napus globally, making the elucidation of its molecular basis critical for breeding new germplasm. Lignocellulose components (including lignin, cellulose, and hemicellulose) play an essential role in the mechanical strength of the stem, and they are regarded as the key determinants of lodging.
